result:
I found 10 of the 150 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings, and fixed all of them. I wrote a script that reads each rule's docstring and works out the expected price. It then compares that with what the function actually returns, across a range of quantities and unit prices (including values that hit the caps and that don't divide evenly) and for negative inputs. After the fixes, all 150 rules match. I also searched the code for odd patterns the script might miss (`round`, float division, extra conditions) and found none.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 33 (marginal) | Capped the eligible amount before applying the percentage, not the discount itself | Compute the discount, then cap it at 30,000 won |
| 41 | Discount started at 6 units | Starts at 5 units |
| 50 | Discount started at 13 units | Starts at 12 units |
| 63 | Cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 won, so discounts between 30,000 and 60,000 weren't capped | Always cap at 30,000 won |
| 113 | Capped the price at 10,000 won before applying the percentage | Cap the discount at 10,000 won |
| 122 | Capped the price at 50,000 won before applying the percentage | Cap the discount at 50,000 won |
| 126 | Rounded the discount (`round(... / 100)`) | Round down to the won (`// 100`) |
| 136 | Applied 9% | Applies 8% |
| 143 (whole) | Discounted only the units above the threshold (marginal style) | Discounts the full amount |
| 148 | Applied 4% | Applies 3% |

STATUS: DONE
